newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-BEATEN KAFELNIKOV PESSIMISTIC ABOUT FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BEATEN KAFELNIKOV PESSIMISTIC ABOUT FRANCE.

text.p: World number four Yevgeny Kafelnikov suffered a heavy blow ahead of his French Open title defence when he was knocked out of the Italian Open by Spain's Alberto Berasategui on Thursday.

Kafelnikov lasted less than hour against his unseeded opponent, losing 6-3 6-2 and then said it "would take a miracle" to retain the French crown at Roland Garros. The grand slam tournament starts on Monday week.

The Russian is desperately short of match practice after a three-month lay-off with a broken finger in his right hand, and his error-strewn performance against Berasategui earned him a chorus of boos from the Foro Italico faithful.
His fifth successive defeat to 1994 French Open runner-up Berasategui means Italians have seen their premier tennis tournament lose its top five seeds in just three rounds.

The world's top two players Pete Sampras and Michael Chang, both American, were eliminated in the first round, and Austria's Thomas Muster and Dutchman Richard Krajicek -- last year's finalists -- were knocked out on Wednesday.
Another seed, number 11 Albert Costa of Spain, also went out on Thursday to Marc-Kevin Goellner of Germany 6-4 3-6 6-4. That left just six seeds in the tournament.
In five matches against the Spaniard, Kafelnikov has failed to take a set. "I just cannot find the key to his game," he said. "He's just too difficult for me."
At times, it seemed that all Berasategui had to do to win the match was keep the ball in court.
In the second set, Kafelnikov hardly won a point on the Spaniard's serve, was broken twice before blasting the first match-point far beyond the baseline.
Kafelnikov has played just six tournaments this season after breaking his finger on a punch-bag in January, and, despite reaching the semifinal at Hamburg last week, admits he is in poor shape.
"This is my sixth consecutive week of tennis and, at this point, my body is getting tired," he said.
"After the injury, I decided to play as many matches as possible to defend my ranking. If I lose at the French Open, I will be out of the top 10."
The tournament's top seed is now number six Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia, who plays German Boris Becker for a place in the quarter-finals later on Thursday.
